skills.name: Belgian Congo: independence and the outbreak of crisis

note.text: The Belgian Congo became independent on 30 June 1960. Colonial inequalities, weak preparation for African control of key institutions and disputes over authority made the transition difficult. An army mutiny, Belgian military intervention and secessionist movements rapidly deepened the crisis. Katanga declared secession in July. Congolese rivalries interacted with foreign political and economic interests in a Cold War setting. No single label explains every cause, and the crisis is not proof that Africans were inherently unable to govern.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to connect a rapid transfer, army mutiny, secession and foreign intervention without reducing the crisis to one cause. Builds on: varied colonial transitions and limits of constitutional transfer. Leads to: the Congo crisis’s effects and post-independence instability.

sections.heading: Follow the evidence and examples
sections.text: The army mutiny began in early July {1960}; Katanga’s secession under Moïse Tshombe was announced on {11} July. The Congolese government requested UN assistance, and the Security Council established ONUC on {14} July. These connected developments should be distinguished from Congo’s legal independence and from the operation’s later outcomes.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Identify actor, action, place and period before explaining a relationship. Use the practice text only for the claim it supports. Distinguish a cause, an event and an outcome; compare authentic sources before treating an interpretation as established. A sequence alone does not prove that every later outcome was inevitable.

cards.idea: Check a claim against the sequence, setting and limits of the evidence.
example: Legal independence guaranteed that every state institution was already stable. Correction: Sovereignty and institutional capacity are different questions.
The mutiny was simply a peaceful constitutional election. Correction: It involved a breakdown within the armed forces.
Secession meant only changing a minister within the same central government. Correction: It challenged the state’s territorial unity.
No foreign actor was involved in the Congo crisis. Correction: Outside involvement is explicitly part of its history.
